title: Lahaina Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: December 13, 2023

issues.title: Moving fire survivors off FEMA interim housing

recap.headline: Lahaina weekly recovery update: debris removal sign-ups, rebuild permits, housing and ash
recap.in_60_seconds: Maui County, State and federal agencies held their weekly Lahaina community meeting to update fire survivors on recovery. Thirteen officials and one nonprofit researcher presented; there was no public testimony, and questions were taken one-on-one at stations after the talks. About 60% of the 2,176 burned properties (1,275) have signed up for government debris removal, and Public Works urged owners to avoid the costly alternate program. The County plans to send an expedited rebuild permitting ordinance to the Council before month's end. FEMA reported 50 households placed through direct leases, and the Department of Health released Lahaina ash results. The final debris disposal site is still undecided, with a community meeting set for Monday, December 18, and the timing of the Wahikuli sewer line remains unknown.

parts.title: Opening and MEMA leadership transition
presented: The meeting format is presentations first, then speakers take questions at stations around the room.
The search for a permanent MEMA administrator began with 16 applicants and is down to 5 finalists; an assessment center will be held the next day.
The Mayor hopes to announce the new administrator by early next week.
The former interim MEMA administrator received a plaque thanking him for his work after the August 8, 2023 wildfires.

next.what: Assessment of the five MEMA administrator finalists
Decision on the next MEMA administrator

parts.title: Department of Education school dust and air sampling
parts.presenter: Department of Education environmental health staff
presented: Wipe samples for metals are taken every other week in three classrooms and one outdoor spot at Princess Nāhiʻenaʻena Elementary and Lahaina Intermediate, plus air samples for asbestos.
Sampling was done October 6, October 23, November 6, November 20 and December 4.
The method detects lead down to 10 micrograms per square foot, the clearance level for floors.
So far no metal contamination has been found in the schools.

next.what: Sampling resumes after the holiday break

parts.title: Debris removal rights of entry outreach
parts.presenter: County Department of Management staff; member of the Mayor's advisory team
presented: 1,275 right-of-entry forms have been submitted out of 2,176 properties, about 60%.
Submitting a right of entry is the first step to sign up for government-sponsored debris removal.
The advisory team member said the remaining roughly 42% could cost more money and time and hold back the next step for the community.
He urged neighbors to reach owners who moved away, speak other languages or struggle with the fine print.

parts.title: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers debris removal and temporary school
parts.presenter: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Recovery Field Office commander
presented: 173 properties deemed too unsafe by the EPA are being passed to the Corps, which will make them safe in Phase 2 and then work with the County on a reentry window for owners.
Phase 1 property assessments, including archaeological review, are over 90% complete.
Neighborhoods with the highest share of rights of entry will be cleared first, following County priorities.
The temporary King Kamehameha III Elementary school near the airport remains on schedule.

next.what: Announcement of reentry plan for deferred unsafe properties

parts.title: Public Works rebuild permitting
presented: The director urged owners to use the right-of-entry program instead of the alternate private program; one alternate work plan runs 300 pages with over a dozen consultants.

There is no special rebuild permit process yet; an ordinance for an expedited process for fire-affected parcels is planned to go to the Council before the end of the month, and an RFP is out for a consultant to run an emergency permit center.
Temporary structures and dwellings are allowed, and the rules are being refined.
The County will consider reissuing building permits for homes built within five years before the fire.

next.what: Expedited fire rebuild permitting ordinance sent to County Council
next.when: before the end of the month

parts.title: Environmental Management: sewer and final debris site
presented: Damage assessment is underway on 95,000 linear feet of sewer line in Lahaina.
Timing of the Wahikuli sewer line depends on EPA support and is not yet known.
Owners must certify their sewer lateral is undamaged, or repair it, before connecting.
The temporary debris storage site is an Army Corps project; the final disposition site is a separate County project.

next.what: Community meeting on the final debris disposition site at Lahaina Civic Center, 5:30 to 7 p.m.

parts.title: Department of Water Supply restoration
presented: Areas 1, 2, 3A and 3B have drinkable water.
Areas 4A to 4D are taking longer than expected because of more service laterals and debris; completion is hoped for by end of December or the first week of January.
Water is back but not drinkable in Wahikuli, below Kanakea Loop to Kilauea Street, and down to Puamana; it can be used for toilets, laundry, lukewarm showers and irrigation.

next.when: end of December or first week of January

parts.title: Department of Health: ash, air quality and behavioral health
parts.presenter: Deputy Director for Environmental Health; Deputy Director of Health
presented: Lahaina ash results are posted online: arsenic was 11 times the action level (Kula ash was 100 times), lead 2 times and cobalt 5 times; the main risk is from swallowing ash.
There are 58 PurpleAir sensors, 32 in Lahaina and 25 in Kula; Kula air samples showed no asbestos and very low metals.
Suicide and substance-abuse death rates through November have not changed from before the fire, and crisis line calls have not surged.
In a recent survey, 80% of respondents knew how to access mental health services.

parts.title: FEMA housing update and outside ash expert
parts.presenter: FEMA official; Wildfire Conservancy executive director
presented: Just over 2,600 households remain in hotels; FEMA wants at least 3,000 units from more than 13,000 vacant short-term rentals.
3,768 households received initial rental assistance; 50 households are placed through direct leases with 103 more units expected by mid-December; group sites are possible if units are not found.
The FEMA and SBA application deadline was December 11, with a 60-day FEMA grace period and a 45-day SBA grace period.
The nonprofit expert said fugitive ash risk fades after 70 to 90 days or about three-quarters of an inch of rain, and both thresholds have passed.

parts.title: Announcements and Mayor's closing on final debris site
presented: No community meetings on December 27 or January 3; regular meetings are Tuesdays in Kula and Wednesdays in Lahaina.
The Mayor called mental health the County's number one concern.
The Mayor asked residents for feedback on the final debris site: the Olowalu option would hold only Lahaina debris, while the Central Maui Landfill would mix it with other garbage.
He said several sites were considered and urgency is about getting debris off the land and out of the air and water.

bills.name: Expedited fire rebuild permitting ordinance
bills.what: Would create a separate, faster building permit process for fire-affected parcels.

open_questions.question: When will the Wahikuli sewer line be available, so owners can decide about converting cesspools or septic systems?
Where will the final Lahaina debris disposal site be, and do residents want it kept on the West Side?
Will building permit fees be waived for fire rebuilds?
Who will be named the permanent MEMA administrator?

not_on_tracker.topic: Debris removal rights of entry and Army Corps cleanup order
not_on_tracker.why: About 40% of burned properties have not signed up, which could slow cleanup of whole neighborhoods.

not_on_tracker.topic: Final disposal site for Lahaina fire debris
not_on_tracker.why: Residents care whether debris and remains stay on the West Side or go to the Central Maui Landfill mixed with other waste.

not_on_tracker.topic: Restoring drinkable water and sewer service in Lahaina
not_on_tracker.why: Owners need water and working sewer lines before they can return or rebuild.

not_on_tracker.topic: Dust and metal testing at Lahaina schools
not_on_tracker.why: Families want to know their children's classrooms are safe from fire contamination.
Officials said the community needs stable long-term emergency leadership.
The Mayor called mental health the County's top concern for survivors.

moments.who: Maui County Director of Public Works
moments.quote: We do have a process for temporary structures, temporary dwellings.
moments.about: Public Works said early in the recovery that the county already had a process for temporary dwellings on fire-affected lots and was refining those rules for the period between debris cleanup and rebuilding.

moments.who: Maui County Director of Environmental Management
moments.quote: Once that's deemed up and running, you have to certify that your sewer lateral is not damaged. If it is damaged, then you would need to repair that, and then you can tie into our sewer line once we clear the use of that sewer line in the roadway.
moments.about: Environmental Management explained the wastewater requirement for owners who want temporary structures on their Lahaina lots: the sewer line to the home must be certified undamaged before connecting.
